content.text:
# Hartwell Supply Co.: what you're looking at

Hartwell is a family-held HVAC/R distributor: about 150 people, twelve branches (Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati, Dayton, Toledo, Akron, Indianapolis, Fort Wayne, Louisville, Lexington, Troy MI and Pittsburgh), selling equipment, parts, refrigerant and supplies to heating and cooling contractors. The records run from 2016 to 2025.

**Its systems, each a separate database copied into the warehouse:**
- **ERP** (`erp_*`): customers and their account managers, the sales reps, products and vendors, sales orders and their lines (how each order arrived and who keyed it), purchase orders, transfers between branches, and returns.
- **Warehouse management** (`wms_*`): every stock movement (opening balances, receipts, sales, transfers, returns) and goods receipts. Stock on hand isn't stored anywhere: it's the running total of the movements.
- **Accounting** (`finance_*`): invoices and their lines, credit memos, customer payments, vendor bills and their lines, and vendor payments.
- **CRM** (`crm_*`): calls and emails to customer service, as logged by whoever took them; and the reps' quotes, with each quote's lines, its outcome (won, lost or expired), a loss reason when the rep entered one, and the order a won quote became.
- **External** (`external_*`): real monthly heating and cooling degree days and residential building permits for each branch's county.

**Days.** `day` is an operating day, about 21 a month; `dim_date` gives the calendar date.

**What isn't here:** profitability by customer, rep or branch; why a return happened; whether an order was keyed correctly; whether a vendor bill was right. Like any real business, those have to be worked out from the records, and some of them can't be.

WITH l AS (
 SELECT l.line_id, l.order_id, l.sku, l.fulfilment, l.qty_ordered, l.qty_shipped, l.unit_price, o.day, o.customer_id, o.branch
 FROM erp_sales_order_lines l JOIN erp_sales_orders o USING(order_id)),
w AS (
 SELECT *, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id, sku ORDER BY day RANGE BETWEEN 1 FOLLOWING AND 10 FOLLOWING) AS n_next10,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE qty_shipped>0) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id, sku ORDER BY day RANGE BETWEEN 1 FOLLOWING AND 10 FOLLOWING) AS n_next10_shipped,
  count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id, sku ORDER BY day RANGE BETWEEN 0 PRECEDING AND 0 FOLLOWING) AS n_sameday
 FROM l)
SELECT fulfilment, count(*) n, avg((n_next10>0)::int) share_reorder10, avg((n_next10_shipped>0)::int) share_reorder10_shipped, avg((n_sameday>1)::int) share_sameday_other
FROM w WHERE day <= 2510 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

input.content:
# H2 notes
- q247: re-order (any line) same customer+SKU within 1-10 days: short 9.34% (n=153,499, day<=2510); shipped re-order only 5.99% vs stock baseline 6.27%. Gap between any vs shipped = repeat shorts (stock-out persists).
- q249 (days 253-2268): shipped re-order 10d short 6.30% vs stock 6.26%; 63d 24.9% vs 22.5%; 252d 40.9% vs 44.0%. Pre-short 10d rate 8.0%. No backorder bump.
- q250: same-order cover by stock/transfer line same SKU: 352 of 155,280. Dead end for "filled by transfer".
- q251: WMS on-hand at branch before order day: zero for 134,229; no history 11,653; >= ordered 6,386; partial 3,012. Shorts are real stock-outs mostly. 6,386 shorts with stock on hand = odd (allocation? timing), not pursued.
- q252: per-year no uplift; category-level 10d re-buy ~66-74% for both short and stock -> uninformative about substitution.
- q254: customer-SKU qty after/before 252d: short 1.033, stock 1.010 -> no lasting loss of that SKU's business. "Customers buy less afterwards" NOT supported.
- q256: branches flat. Equipment short re-order 1.0% vs 2.6% baseline; supplies 11.5 vs 7.5, parts 9.9 vs 6.9, refrigeration 9.8 vs 6.4 -> small recovery 3-4 pts for non-equipment.
- q258: special order within 30d after short: ~0. Equipment = 73,752 shorts, 18.5M of 26.6M short GM all years.
- q263/q267: equipment substitute same tonnage: same order 19.2% vs 24.1% for stock lines; next 10d 27.6% vs 31.5%. No substitution signal.
- q265 sizing: GM (standard cost) of shorts not reshipped in 10d, avg 2017-2024 = 2,165,946.53/yr. Upper bound; 2016 start-up, 2025 end-effects excluded.

content.text:
The hypothesis holds: short lines (lines that shipped nothing because stock was out) are almost never followed by a re-order, so most of them look like lost sales rather than delayed ones. At most about **$2.17M a year** in margin isn't recovered (2,165,946.53, average for 2017–2024 at standard cost, q265). I've saved `prediction.json`, `notes.md` and `finding.json` (F6).

**What the records show**
- **No re-order bump.** Only 6.30% of short lines are followed within 10 operating days by a shipped order from the same customer for the same SKU, at any branch. That's the same as the 6.26% repeat rate after ordinary filled lines (103,538 short lines vs 1,880,966 filled, days 253–2268, q249). The rate is flat in every year and at every branch (q252, q256).
- **The stock-outs are real.** 134,229 of 155,280 short lines had zero stock on hand at the branch the day before the order (q251).
- **Not covered another way.** 352 short lines had the same SKU filled from stock or by transfer on the same order (q250), and almost none were followed by a special order within 30 days (q258).
- **Equipment carries most of the money.** It accounts for 73,752 short lines and $18.5M of the $26.6M margin on all short lines over ten years. Equipment short lines are re-ordered within 10 days only 1.02% of the time, against 2.59% after a filled equipment line. I found no sign that customers took a same-tonnage substitute instead (q256, q258, q263, q267).
- **Small recovery elsewhere.** Parts, supplies and refrigeration are re-ordered about 3–4 points more often than baseline, so a small share does come back (q256).
- **Not supported:** the hypothesis's second claim, that customers buy less afterwards. Their purchases of that SKU over the following year don't fall: the after/before quantity ratio is 1.033 after short lines vs 1.010 after filled lines (q254). The loss is the single sale, not the account.

**Limits (confidence: medium)**
- **The $2.17M is a ceiling.** It is margin at standard cost (costs never change in these records) on short lines with no re-order within 10 days. 2016 is excluded as a start-up artefact and 2025 because the year is incomplete.
- **Re-order is a heuristic.** Nothing links a short line to a later line, so matching on customer, SKU and time window is the best the data allows.
- **Why the sale was lost is unknown.** The records can't tell a competitor, a cancelled job, a fix outside the ERP or a substitute under another code apart.
- **One loose end.** 6,386 short lines had enough stock on hand, which I couldn't explain.

**Suggested next step:** ask branch staff what actually happens after an equipment short line. Then rank equipment SKUs by short-line margin to set safety stock or automatic transfer rules, and start recording lost sales or backorder links so recovery can be measured.
